problem: The production Netlify build again contained contradictory i18n contracts: an older test and build guard required provider success, while the canonical fallback architecture required provider failure to degrade to runtime translation.
root_cause: Two mutually exclusive prevention rules coexisted. The older fail-closed rule treated build-time translation provider success as production authority; the newer rule correctly treats visible browser-level English output as production authority.
prevention: Build-time static English translation is enrichment, not the terminal production authority.
A deterministic or transient provider failure must return the runtime fallback path and must not abort the whole website build.
Production remains fail-closed at observable browser proof: the actual NL to EN switch must reach /en/prijzen and visibly render English.
Tests may not require STATIC_I18N_PRODUCTION_TRANSLATION_FAILED or STATIC_I18N_PRODUCTION_TRANSLATION_REQUIRED while runtime fallback is canonical.
When prevention rules conflict, reconcile the older test and learning contract instead of reintroducing a previously fixed production blocker.

evidence.symptom: linked main production build failed during build before publication
evidence.conflict: older provider-fatal test contradicted newer runtime-fallback regression test
